article_notes: Retrospective single-time-point study at Onderstepoort (University of Pretoria): 32 dogs with PCR-RLB-confirmed B. rossi (18 uncomplicated, 14 complicated) and 20 healthy controls; all treated with diminazene. 21 serum proteins differed between complicated and uncomplicated dogs (Table 1); all rows are significant by design (FDR <0.05) - non-significant proteins for this comparison are not listed. Proteins mapped to existing canonical markers where one fits (fibrinogen alpha chain, complement components, apoE, transferrin, protein S, prothrombin fragment); others under Proteomics / metabolomics. Timing of sampling relative to diminazene not stated. Cohort likely overlaps other Onderstepoort B. rossi studies (ethics V0034-14).

severity_definitions.label: complicated vs uncomplicated babesiosis
severity_definitions.definition: Complicated if clinical collapse, cerebral signs (seizures, coma) or death within 24 h of admission, or any of: haematocrit <0.15 or >0.5 L/L, urea >13 mmol/L, creatinine >120 umol/L, total bilirubin >30 umol/L, glucose <3.3 mmol/L, lactate >5 mmol/L, band neutrophils >1.5 x 10^9/L. Uncomplicated dogs met none. PCR-RLB confirmed B. rossi mono-infection.
severity_definitions.quote: Dogs were classified as having complicated babesiosis on the basis of clinical signs and clinical pathology. Clinical signs included: clinical signs of collapse, signs of cerebral disease (seizures, coma) or death within 24 h of admission.

associations.marker_as_reported: lactotransferrin (LTF), western blot relative abundance
associations.statistic: western blot normalised to total protein; Kruskal-Wallis with post hoc test
associations.quote: Relative abundance for LTF was significantly different between the control group and complicated babesiosis (P = 0.003), apoE was significantly different between control and uncomplicated babesiosis (P < 0.001), as well as between control and complicated babesiosis (P < 0.001), while beta actin showed significant difference between control and complicated babesiosis (P < 0.001) and between uncomplicated and complicated babesiosis (P = 0.004) (Fig. 7).
associations.location: Results, Validation; Fig. 7A
associations.note: Only the control vs complicated difference is reported as significant; uncomplicated vs complicated not significant by implication. Values in figure only.
